Hi Samira / Kevin —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and suggested next steps so we can align on deployment mode and compliance requirements: 

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Primary workload will process PHI (clinical notes + scheduling data) and needs HIPAA protections + a signed BAA.
- SOC2 Type II evidence required for procurement.
- SSO (SAML/SSO) for internal users; customer-managed KMS and ability to isolate logs are preferred.
- Data residency: US-only, ideally us-east region.
- Audit log retention and exportability required for audits (7 years is ideal from your side).

Deployment options (high-level tradeoffs):
- Hosted API (fastest): We can sign a BAA and apply tenant-level controls; good for low to medium volume PHI when you allow hosted managed encryption. Offers fastest time-to-prod but less isolation than Dedicated/Private.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity / VPC): Dedicated GPU pools with network isolation and optional customer-managed KMS. Recommended for predictable throughput and stronger data isolation while remaining managed by Redwood.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full private deployment (customer VPC or on-prem) for maximum control — recommended when policy/regulator requires customer-managed networking or strict in-country hosting.

Attachments I am sending with this message: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (SOC2 Type II report), BAA_Draft_Redwood.pdf (draft BAA), redwood-deployment-options.pdf (short tech/ops comparison).

Proposed next steps:
1) Please review the attached SOC2 and BAA draft.
2) Quick technical deep-dive with our infra/security team (we suggest Mon Mar 22, 10:00 AM PT) — duration ~45 minutes.
3) If you can share answers to the short questionnaire below ahead of the call, we can tailor the deep-dive:
   - Estimated monthly token volume / peak concurrency
   - Required retention period for logs and where they must be stored
   - Whether you require customer-managed KMS and/or SSO identity provider (IdP) details

Happy to jump on a call this week to walk through.

Thanks,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Samira — thanks for the questions, answers below. I've attached a short pen test summary and the SOC2 cover page which shows the audit period.

1) Hosted API + PHI: Hosted is allowed if a BAA is in place and we provision a tenant with the appropriate controls (data encryption, restricted retention, access controls). For higher risk or required network isolation we recommend Dedicated. Ultimately the choice depends on your security profile and throughput needs.

2) Residency & logs: Yes — for both Hosted (tenant-scoped) and Dedicated we can restrict data to US regions; Dedicated and Private give stronger guarantees. Audit logs can be exported in JSON/CSV; we will include the schema in the deep-dive.

3) Customer-managed KMS (CMK): CMK is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments today. For Hosted, we offer managed keys; BYOK for Hosted is not generally available unless we arrange a private deployment variant. If CMK is a hard requirement, we should plan for Dedicated or Private.

4) SOC2 report: The attached Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf covers the period Jan 1, 2026 - Oct 31, 2026 and includes CC1-CC7 control categories relevant to security and availability.

5) Pen testing: We run annual third-party pentests and a summary is attached (PenTest_Summary_2026.pdf). For enterprise customers we can provide redacted findings and remediation timelines under NDA.

Additional notes:
- SSO: SAML/OIDC integrations are supported across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Audit retention: configurable; we can set a retention policy that meets your 7-year requirement, though for very long retention we typically recommend Dedicated or Private to keep costs and data locality predictable.
- Data flow diagram & HIPAA checklist: attaching a short checklist in the deep-dive pack; we will bring a sample data flow diagram to the technical call.

Proposed deep-dive: Mon Mar 22, 10:00 AM PT — I will invite our infra lead (Marissa) and security engineer (Neha). Does that work for you?

Thanks,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer
